narrative.overview:
An editorial exposure sheet gives real software and photographs the weight of tangible objects. Warm parchment and deep navy share a restrained copper interaction signal. Broad local typography, fine rules and generous asymmetric spacing make the work legible before optional movement begins.

The first viewport pairs the exact live paper headline with a real software screenshot. The crumpled-paper image and held rotations remain a supporting material; screenshot scale, curved project surfaces and scroll-fanning photographic prints carry the larger choreography. Both routes share the same material system. The active surface contract is `.impeccable/surfaces/editorial-studio.md`.

Current theme override: creamy beige light mode and user-supplied Solarin gunmetal/sapphire/platinum/peach/tan dark mode; older cobalt wording is historical.
keyCharacteristics: Actual software evidence shares the opening viewport with identity.
Cobalt, cream and orange remain coherent across both themes.
Anybody headings pair with Instrument Sans reading and controls.
Real crumpled paper holds twelve rotation poses over three seconds.
Image continuity connects introduction, reel, workspace and photographic portal.
Native controls, visible focus and static fallbacks preserve every content path.

rules.name: The Shared Materials Rule
rules.body: Apply the selected theme across both routes; reserve copper for action, focus and selected feedback. Preserve original image colors.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Anybody carries expressive headings; Instrument Sans carries reading and controls. Retained alternative font assets are not additional type roles.

rules.name: The Object Depth Rule
rules.body: Keep editorial reading surfaces flat; concentrate depth on real screenshots, photographic prints and textured paper.

dos: Do preserve exact factual content, actual screenshots and all 253 archive photographs.
Do keep named native controls, copper focus and a clear parent path through project branches.
Do gate optional movement by reduced motion and Effects preferences and retain static image fallbacks.
Do use the real crumpled-paper assets and held rotations as a supporting title material.
donts: Don't require motion, hover, WebGL or a loading gate to reach the work.
Don't substitute generated artwork or generic equal cards for actual project and photographic evidence.
Don't describe the paper as polygon-cut geometry or continuously interpolated floating strips.
Don't mechanically invert photographs or alter originals when updating the archive.
